name: Pelatiah
overview: Pelatiah is a male figure from the tribe of Judah, identified uniquely as the son of Hananiah. His presence is briefly noted in the genealogical records of 1 Chronicles 3:21. Beyond his lineage, the biblical text offers no additional details or notable events concerning his life.
namesAndTitles: The name Pelatiah means "Yahweh rescues," reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew understanding of God's saving power. This proper name underscores a divine attribute but is not indicated as being given directly by God in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Pelatiah as the son of Hananiah, establishing a direct father-son relationship. There are no other family connections or relationships mentioned in the biblical text beyond this.
scriptureSignificance: Pelatiah's significance lies primarily in his place within the genealogical lineage of Judah, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:21. His mention contributes to the biblical record of God's providential preservation of the Davidic line, which is foundational to the Messianic promises fulfilled in Christ. Though not elaborated upon, his inclusion affirms God's faithfulness in maintaining the covenantal line through successive generations.
